question: Which of the following methods is used to calculate national income by summing up the total spending on final goods and services in an economy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Expenditure method**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Expenditure method** is used to calculate national income by summing up the total spending on final goods and services in an economy.
 
• It includes the expenditures made by households, businesses, government, and net exports (exports minus imports).
 
• This method is one of the primary approaches to measure the overall economic activity of a country.
 
• The formula for the Expenditure method is: **GDP = C + I + G + (X - M)**, where C is consumption, I is investment, G is government spending, and (X - M) is net exports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Value-added method** calculates national income by adding the value added at each stage of production.
 
• The **Output method** measures the total value of goods and services produced in an economy.
 
• The **Income method** sums up all the incomes earned by individuals and businesses, including wages, profits, rents, and interest.
 
• Each of these methods provides a different perspective on the economic activity and can be used to cross-verify the accuracy of the national income calculations.
